panels.text: You press send. Your mail client hands the message to a mail server.
That server resolves the domain after the @ using DNS. The answer, an MX record, lists the mail exchange servers for that domain.
The message goes by SMTP to that server, sometimes forwarded through other relays. Each one adds a Received line to the header.
The twist: nobody has to be online at once. Email works store-and-forward, and the recipient picks it up from a mailbox later.

probes.question: What do MX records list?
options: The mail exchange servers for a domain

probes.question: True or false: sender and recipient must both be online at the same moment for email to work.

claims.claim: Your mail client hands the message to a mail server (submission agent)
claims.quote: to send the message content to the local mail submission agent

claims.claim: The server resolves the domain after the @ using DNS
claims.quote: The MSA resolves a domain name to determine the fully qualified domain name of the mail server

claims.claim: The answer is an MX record listing the mail exchange servers (probe 1)
claims.quote: responds with any MX records listing the mail exchange servers for that domain

claims.claim: The message goes by SMTP, sometimes forwarded through other relays
claims.quote: This server may need to forward the message to other MTAs before the message reaches the final message delivery agent

claims.claim: Each relay adds a Received line to the header
claims.quote: Every time an MTA receives an email message, it adds a Received trace header field to the top of the header of the message

claims.claim: Email is store-and-forward; nobody has to be online at once (probe 2: false)
claims.quote: Neither the users nor their computers are required to be online simultaneously

claims.claim: The recipient picks it up from a mailbox later
claims.quote: The MDA delivers it to the mailbox of user bob.
